resolutions.researcher_notes: OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (recovered via Wayback per known gotcha; live opec.org URL redirects to homepage/403, confirmed dead — recovered snapshot 200s and pdftotext-extracted locally, listing 'Sahel/km-81.5, Sirte Oil, 49 miles, 30in, 19,541,206 (1,000 scm/yr)' under the Libya section, dated 2011) lists the line as an active entry in the operating gas-transport network, i.e. status context supports 'operating' even though the literal word doesn't appear (per status-inference convention). Independently, Sirte Oil Company's own 2012 procurement notice (yumpu-hosted tender document, ref TP-210341SL) solicits 'Consultancy Agreement for Intelligent Pigging of 30" Gas Pipeline from Sahl Field to KM 81.5' — a live in-service line undergoing routine inline inspection, which corroborates active operating status a year after the OPEC data point. Two independent sources, both context-inferred rather than literal status statements.

Both sources explicitly identify this as a gas line: OPEC ASB Table 4.10 is titled 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' and lists the Sahel/km-81.5 row within it; Sirte Oil's 2012 tender explicitly calls it a '30" Gas Pipeline from Sahl Field to KM 81.5'. Two independent, explicit, matching statements.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10, Libya section, row 'Sahel/km-81.5, Sirte Oil, 49 [miles], 30 [in], 19,541,206 [1,000 scm/yr]' — 19,541,206 thousand scm/yr = 19.541 bcm/yr, matching GEM's 19.54 bcm/y almost exactly. Confirmed by downloading the Wayback snapshot and running pdftotext locally (row is on the physical PDF page reached via a table split across pages 75-76; live opec.org PDF link is dead per the known gotcha, so this is the recovered Wayback URL). Searched Libya Herald, Libya Observer, Sirte Oil/NOC pages, Zawya, and Oil & Gas Journal for a second independent capacity figure for this specific segment and found none — the Sirte in-house network's internal segment-level capacities are not otherwise published. Single source; tier medium.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 lists the Sahel/km-81.5 segment at 49 miles = 78.86 km, matching GEM's 79.00 km almost exactly. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Sirte Oil's own 2012 pigging-tender document (yumpu doc 8653717) describes the same-named route ('30" Gas Pipeline from Sahl Field to KM 81.5') as 'approximate length 55 km' — noticeably shorter than the OPEC/GEM figure. Could reflect a different measured stretch (e.g. the piggable run between launcher/receiver traps, which is often shorter than the full as-built centerline), a rough tender estimate vs. surveyed length, or the tender covering only part of the line. Treating OPEC ASB (49 mi / 78.86 km, near-exact match to GEM's 79.00 km) as the supporting ref since it aligns with the existing GEM value, but flagging the 55 km figure for a human to weigh — it's plausible the true pipe run is shorter than 79 km if OPEC's mileage double-counts a routing or shares mileage with an adjacent segment. Single source for the 79 km figure; tier medium.

Both sources give an exact, matching diameter: OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 lists the Sahel/km-81.5 row at 30 inches; Sirte Oil's 2012 tender document independently and explicitly specifies a '30" Gas Pipeline from Sahl Field to KM 81.5'. Two independent sources, exact match to GEM's 30.00 in.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 lists the Sahel/km-81.5 line under its 'Libya' country section (operator Sirte Oil), directly supporting Start/EndCountryOrArea = Libya. The Sirte Oil tender document independently confirms the operator is a Libyan state company (tender priced in LYD, Libyan Dinar) but the raw page text didn't literally return the string 'Libya' on substring check, so it's used only as supporting context, not counted as a fully independent confirmation for this cell. Both fields (Start/EndCountryOrArea) are country-level only in the brief — no town/prefecture values to verify — km-81.5 and Sahl/Sahel field are both landmarks on the Sirte Basin gas-gathering network per all sources found.

The pipeline is operated by Sirte Oil Company per OPEC ASB (owner/operator column); GEM's Owner1 value is the parent, 'Libyan National Oil Corp' at 100%. Two independent sources confirm Sirte Oil is a wholly state-owned subsidiary of Libya's National Oil Corporation: Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article states it became 'a national firm belonging to the National Oil Corporation fully owned by the State' after Esso Standard's 1981 withdrawal; the US Treasury (OFAC) press release 'Treasury Identifies 14 Companies Owned by Libya's National Oil Corporation' names Sirte Oil Company among NOC's owned subsidiaries. Two independent, non-GEM sources supporting the 100% NOC ownership chain.
